# Platonism quotes

Platonism treats intelligible forms—especially the Good—as more real than shifting appearances, and education as an ascent of the soul.

30 passages · 7 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Plato’s dialogues and later Platonic schools explore justice, love, knowledge, and political order through dialectic. This archive page gathers English passages tagged to Platonic lineages.

## Historical notes

From the Academy through Middle and Neoplatonism into Renaissance and modern revivals, Platonism remains a standing option in metaphysics and ethics.

## Core ideas

-   Forms explain sameness amid change.
-   The Good orients knowledge and politics.
-   Dialectic educates desire as well as intellect.
-   Love can be a ladder from particular beauty to the Beautiful.

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Plutarch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plutarch) , [Boethius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/boethius) , [Plotinus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plotinus) , [Iris Murdoch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/iris-murdoch) , [Damascius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/damascius) , [Synesius of Cyrene](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/synesius-of-cyrene)

## FAQ

### What is Platonism?

It is the family of views descending from Plato that privilege intelligible reality, dialectic, and the ethical centrality of the good.

### Is Platonism only Plato?

No. Later Platonists develop the tradition; this page includes related Platonic school labels in the archive.
